newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOLANA SEES NATO-RUSSIA ACCORD POSSIBLE BY JULY.
newsitem.headline: SOLANA SEES NATO-RUSSIA ACCORD POSSIBLE BY JULY.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Wednesday the alliance could reach an accord with Russia by the time it convenes for a July 8-9 summit in Madrid.

Russia, in a major change of policy, said on Wednesday it would open talks with NATO on a new security partnership between the former Cold War adversaries despite its deep hostility to alliance plans to expand eastwards.

"We are working with tremendous diligence and yearning to reach that great accord between NATO and Russia. I think we are going to reach it," Solana said in an interview with Spanish state television.
"By the summit in Madrid, I think we will have it on track and possibly resolved."

Solana has been authorised to lead the talks with the Russians and said earlier in Brussels NATO wanted to enter formal discussions as quickly as possible for the good of the entire continent. Negotiations could begin in early January.
Moscow has not dropped its opposition to the North Atlantic Treaty Organsation's plans to take in former Kremlin Warsaw Pact allies in eastern and central Europe.
But Moscow did set aside a previous demand that NATO put enlargement on ice before the start of any negotiations.
The offer came one day after the 16 alliance foreign ministers named July 8-9 as the date for a summit in Madrid to invite some former communist countries to open accession talks.
